newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES SOFTER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET LIQUID, RATES SOFTER.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted softer in Wednesday's liquid market, dealers said.
"The market is very flush at the moment and rates are quite depressed," commented one dealer.
Dealers said trade was going on as usual despite a three-week-old strike by Zimbabwe's junior doctors and nurses which has paralysed the country's health system.
On Wednesday, discount houses were buying central bank treasury bills at a steady 19.36 percent but were re-selling them at a lower 19.10 percent from Tuesday's 19.15 percent.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold at 20 and 19.50 percent down from 20.25 and 20 percent while bankers acceptances eased to 19.85 percent from 20 percent (buying) but were selling unchanged at 19.25 percent.
Call money fluctuated between 18.75 and 19 percent in a market which opened Z$990.3 million up compared to Tuesday's Z$284.9 million surplus.
